object_context: Fixed-cutoff/infinite-volume spectral-visibility bridge for the Yang–Mills spectral lane: determine the weakest exact hypotheses under which a common exponential Euclidean-time covariance rate on a gauge-invariant source family whose vacuum-generated states are dense/cyclic in the physical excited-state Hilbert space forces the full positive transfer-matrix spectrum above the vacuum below a common one-step ratio q<1, hence a positive Hamiltonian gap in lattice units. This child repairs the hidden-state failure F-YM-S1A-RESTRICTED-SOURCE-HIDDEN-STATE; it does not address weak-coupling RG transport, a->0 physical scaling, or continuum existence.
structural_coordinates: Work inside one reflection-positive lattice Yang–Mills/infinite-volume Euclidean theory for which a positive self-adjoint one-step transfer matrix T and vacuum Omega are already legitimately reconstructed; no stochastic Langevin generator may substitute for T.

For a centered time-zero gauge-invariant source f, the target bridge requires an exact identification of its Euclidean time-translation covariance with a transfer-matrix moment <psi_f,T^n psi_f> (up to a fixed support-separation offset that is negligible in nth-root asymptotics).

The prior YM-S1a calibration proves that a common rate on a non-dense source-generated sector can miss the true first excitation; source density/cyclicity is therefore a load-bearing hypothesis rather than a cosmetic strengthening.

For a positive self-adjoint contraction T, each vector psi has a positive spectral measure mu_psi and <psi,T^n psi>=integral lambda^n dmu_psi(lambda); nth-root asymptotics constrain the supremum of the spectral support seen by psi.

If a dense subset D of Omega-perp has spectral support contained in [0,q] for one q<1, closedness of the spectral projection E_T([0,q])H upgrades sourcewise exclusion to the whole excited-state Hilbert space.

Shen-Zhu-Zhu Corollary 1.6 gives, in its explicit strong-coupling regime, one exponential distance exponent c_N shared across smooth cylinder functions, while the prefactor depends on support sizes and function norms; fixed multiplicative prefactors disappear under nth-root asymptotics.

The SZZ theorem is stated for covariance under the infinite-volume Euclidean lattice measure and distance between supports; using it as a transfer-matrix bound requires a separate time-direction/reflection-positivity binding and a proof that translating a fixed source n time steps gives support distance n+O(1).

Gauge-invariant spin-network/Peter-Weyl constructions provide fixed-graph orthonormal/spanning families for compact gauge groups, but fixed-graph kinematic completeness is not automatically density of the exact source class in the infinite-volume Osterwalder-Schrader physical Hilbert space.

The source class used for density must lie inside, or be approximable by, the smooth cylinder class to which the common-rate correlation theorem applies; a complete basis outside the controlled regularity class would not close the bridge.

Even a successful fixed-cutoff strong-coupling transfer-gap theorem leaves G5 RG transport, G6 physical lattice-spacing scaling and G7 continuum spectral identification open; an O(1) lattice-unit exponent at fixed strong coupling is not the Clay continuum mass gap.
equivalent_formulations: Spectral-support formulation: find q<1 and a dense D subset Omega-perp such that every psi in D has spectral measure supported in [0,q]; conclude Spec(T|Omega-perp) subset [0,q].

Moment formulation: for one q<1 and dense D subset Omega-perp, prove limsup_{n->infinity}<psi,T^n psi>^(1/n) <= q for every nonzero psi in D, with T positive; conclude the same full spectral exclusion.

Euclidean-source formulation: prove one exponential time-separation rate m>0 for a gauge-invariant local source class whose reconstructed vectors are dense in Omega-perp, while allowing source-dependent finite prefactors; identify q=e^{-m}.
Hamiltonian formulation at unit lattice spacing: with T=e^{-H} and vacuum energy zero, prove Spec(H|Omega-perp) subset [m,infinity) from the dense-source common-rate condition.
solved_analogues: The exact three-state YM-S1a calibration becomes a solved positive/negative known-answer pair after adding the missing source B: with sources spanning both excited eigenvectors, the slowest visible rate equals the true transfer gap.

Standard spectral calculus for a positive self-adjoint contraction converts vector moments <psi,T^n psi> into moments of positive spectral measures and identifies their exponential rate with the top of the spectral support.
near_solved_analogues: Baez 1994 and Burgio et al. 1999 construct spin-network/physical gauge-invariant bases for compact-group gauge theories at fixed graph/lattice, supplying a kinematic model for the density side but not the required infinite-volume OS/source-class binding.

Shen-Zhu-Zhu 2022/2023 prove a common exponential covariance exponent for smooth cylinder functions in an explicit infinite-volume strong-coupling lattice Yang–Mills regime, supplying the rate side but not by itself the transfer-matrix/density identification.

explicit_disanalogies: A common Euclidean covariance exponent is not a Hamiltonian spectral gap until the reflection-positive transfer-moment identity is bound to the same theory.
Fixed-graph or finite-lattice spin-network completeness is not automatically infinite-volume OS Hilbert-space density.
A source-dependent prefactor is not itself fatal to an asymptotic rate, but a source-dependent exponent would be.
A dense source family does not help if the correlation theorem does not cover that family.
A fixed strong-coupling lattice-unit gap is not a physical continuum mass gap and does not solve RG transport or a->0 scaling.

common_abstraction: local measurements see only the modes in their generated observation subspace
global exclusion needs observation coverage plus one common quantitative rate
finite channel-dependent gains do not change asymptotic exponential rates
source_to_target_mapping: uninstrumented room -> spectrally invisible low-energy state
complete sensor coverage -> dense/cyclic source family
common decay ceiling -> common q<1 bound on source spectral support
shared_constraints: missing coverage permits a hidden slow mode
coverage alone without a common quantitative rate is insufficient
common rate on incomplete coverage is insufficient
disanalogies: finite rooms/sensors are not an infinite-dimensional gauge-constrained Hilbert space
ordinary sensor readings need not be positive spectral moments
